## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Digitone (MKI) / Digitone Keys

- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}
- **F5** (F) Never run parsers across device generations (Digitone mk1 device ID 0x0D vs Digitone II, Analog Four gen-1 vs gen-2). `[doc]` {syxgrid} {digi-roll-studio}

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building} (`recovery#ff8f0917`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L37))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB6** The stock restart does not wait for the +Drive or drain the panel link (Digitone mk1 / Keys, OS 1.43 and 1.44; open in stock; worked around by a core). Workaround: elekloader core-dn1 exports `core_restart`, which does both; use it instead of stock's.

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I45** Recovery used on a Digitone MK1 after a logo hang. Cause: the build. Fix: startup menu; not EMPTY RESET or FACTORY RESET. Rules: A2,A36.

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **T3** (needs unit + a USB mod, effort M) Test rule A39 (no EP0 stage of a multiple of 64 bytes) on a small box with a vendor request. The DT2 has the same EHCI-style controller with EP0 max packet 64 and its own EP0 vendor requests (digikit 42), so it is the best candidate
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

## 9. All 49 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] Recovery, used on a unit (digitone-arp-mod, 2026-10-08, OS 1.44): A test build finished its upgrade but hung on the Elektron logo: the logo did not dissolve, with "H" at bottom left and "1.44" at bottom right. The owner held FUNC at power-on, chose TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), and sent stock 1.44 via Transfer's *SYSEX TRANSFER -> OS Upgrade via device startup menu* over DIN (a Rubix22 interface). The unit worked again. EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET are not rollbacks; don't pick them. `[hw]` {dn1-arpmod-e04} — `digitone#7c82fc7f` [hardware/devices/digitone.md:10](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md#L10) · Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / Basics
- [doc] [hw] The Digitone mk1 is a Digitakt mk1 plus six keys, a second ColdFire and an FPGA. taktone runs Digitakt 1.53/1.54 main OS builds on Digitone hardware by replacing only section 3 and adapting the panel, LEDs, codec start-up, autosave GPIO and shutdown copy. Four 1.53-based builds were reported working on hardware. `[hw]` Both main CPUs set up 128 MiB DDR at `0x40000000-0x48000000` (cached and uncached aliases are the same RAM). `[doc]` — `digitone#5d160ac5` [hardware/devices/digitone.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md#L18) · Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
- [hw] How the main CPU drives the second ColdFire (board interface, from taktone-extended, which ran its own engine on it): Reset: PB6 held low. Releasing it starts a serial boot. Upload: the main CPU is DSPI2 slave (eDMA 29, vector 149) and the secondary supplies the clock. Section 6 (a 1,504-byte loader stream; dnfw's section table lists it as 1,492 bytes and "unidentified") loads section 7, which runs at secondary `0x40000400` from entry `0x40000B92`. Shared SRAM: FlexBus, main at `0x10000000`, secondary at `0x00000000`. Native use is below offset `0x7a0`: a 928-byte parameter packet at `0x000-0x39f`, then eight mono voices of 32 signed 32-bit samples at `0x3a0-0x79f`. Handshake: the secondary writes `HO`/`HA`; the main writes 1 to +2 before `B0` to +0. The stock secondary then writes `A5A5` at +4. Render request: a PA4 edge triggers the secondary's DTIM0 capture (vector 96). The secondary signals back through EPORT4 (vector 68). One block of pipeline: ~0.667 ms. Clear stale shared words at start, because they can survive a main reset. Never wait in the audio IRQ for late output, and bound the start-up polling. `[hw]` — `digitone#14f6ecc5` [hardware/devices/digitone.md:21](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md#L21) · Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
- [hw] Two SysEx addressings: the startup menu's OS UPGRADE receiver always expects Digitone-addressed SysEx (device `0x0d`). A running Digitakt-based application expects Digitakt addressing (`0x0a`). So recovery to stock Digitone always goes through the startup menu over DIN. `[hw]` (first install confirmed over USB) — `digitone#3fa3db0b` [hardware/devices/digitone.md:29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md#L29) · Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
- [doc] [hw] Memory: taktone shrinks the native buddy heap from 16 to 8 MiB to reserve `0x4319D6B0-0x4399D6B0` for its runtime, with guard words at both ends. The sample pool (`0x43BAF5F0-0x47BAF640`) and the audio-input ring (`0x47C00000-0x48000000`) stay untouched. This is the same heap-reservation idea as SyntHack's modarea on the Syntakt. `[hw]` (Sophie on the secondary ran on units) / `[doc]` (addresses) — `digitone#652f7eea` [hardware/devices/digitone.md:39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md#L39) · Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
- [hw] The emulator and the unit disagreed: The unit's CPU meter went from ~70 % to ~87 % at idle between two releases, while the emulator's cycle model said the render had become *faster*. Suspects are what the model leaves out: EMAC mode switches (each handler flipped MACSR between integer and fractional, 12 switches per block), DDR bursts for a 24-bit delay line, instruction-cache pressure from inlining, and UI redraws. - [doc] What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re} — `firmware-container#ded70082` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:61](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L61) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)
- [doc] Preamble of the decoded byte stream: u32 container size + u32 content checksum, then the container (magic at offset 8). Container size: DN2 1,743,120, DN1 1,102,352 (the sizes of the file pair dnfw analysed). The content checksum is not a standard algorithm: a running 32-bit sum over big-endian words, each word XORed with its one-based index; trailing bytes that do not fill a word are excluded. Compressed sections carry a header with the stream length and a u32 sum of the stream bytes (padding excluded). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} — `firmware-container#df3a4b13` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:89](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L89) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
- [doc] SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} — `firmware-container#aec8faff` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:90](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L90) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
- [doc] Trailer: the last 32 bytes of the declared container are an HMAC-SHA256 on the first 16-byte boundary at least 4 bytes past the last section (gap zeroed); it covers everything before it, padding included; the key is derived from material inside the image (a printable string in a decompressed section, found in the bootstrap, plus a fixed constant) - never edit that key material, the device likely verifies with its installed copy. DN1 1.42A is unsigned (trailer all zeros). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} — `firmware-container#d4944529` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:91](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L91) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
